messages.author: 2889aa2e61425c8e
messages.subject: Re: Plotting individual replicate FC along with mean point range FC
parts:
Dear Bhavesh,

I am not sure I fully understand your analysis from the description. But the sentence "split the dataframe by replicates and run msstats dataprocess on individual replicates" doesn't sound like a correct thing to do. 

If you are interested in temporal changes, you need to fit the model with all the replicates, and then test the null hypothesis comparing the time points. This can be done by specifying an appropriate contrast.

More generally, hypothesis testing typically focuses on statements regarding the entire populations (i.e., what happens on average over many replicates) as opposed to an individual replicate.

If you had something else in mind, please post your code and (a portion of) an example dataset. Maybe we'll be able to make a more specific comment.

I hope that this helps at least somewhat

Sincerely
OV

Dear Prof. Vitek,

My apologies for the poor explanation. 

 Indeed, you are right and the statistics in the attached figure would still be on the average of all replicates (the big circle with error bars in the above example).

I was wondering if there is a way to grab the data points used to calculate SE for mean foldchange in groupComparison or visualize the spread of all replicates along with the average.


 This is what I tried with control vs treated (2 conditions) PRM data with 4 replicates


raw <- data.frame(read_csv(str_c(rootDir, "/01_MSstats.csv"), na = c("", "NA", "0")))

processedData <- dataProcess(raw, logTrans = 2,
                             normalization = "globalStandards",
                             nameStandards = "x")  

comparison <- matrix(c(1,-1), nrow = 1)
FC <- groupComparison(contrast.matrix = comparison, data = processedData) #this is the average result with proper statistics, until here everything is fine.

 

Now I want to see the spread of data points for each replicate so I tried to split and process individually;

rep1 <- filter(raw, BioReplicate == 1) #replicate 1

rep1dataprocess <- dataProcess(raw, logTrans = 2,

                             normalization = "globalStandards",
                             nameStandards = "x")

Error in setnames(x, value) :

  Can't assign 4 names to a 0 column data.table

For some reason, this 1 replicate dataProcess command seems to work when there are 3 conditions (of course, without SE or significance values), but not with 2 conditions.

Coming back to my question, is there a way to tabulate or visualize all the data points used for calculating meanFC and SE in groupComparison matrix  (irrespective of the number of conditions)?

Thanks a lot!!

Bhavesh
